method: Read-only IDA decompilation, instruction and cross-reference review of the existing database; public documentation used as secondary corroboration.
address_convention: Unslid virtual addresses in this exact 23.6.1 input; not runtime pointers or offsets for another game version.

functions.role: locked orb check with visual side effects
orb pointer exchange and movement setup
phase dispatcher and common update tail
movement and special-state gate before matching

claims.claim: Active spinner cells share a countdown, but the updater visits every active row/cell and applies per-orb eligibility.
claims.implication: Multiple spinners are supported by native behavior. Shared countdown does not imply identical or fixed relative colors after orb movement.

claims.claim: A spinner recolors only when its current orb has state 0 and its lock bit is clear.
claims.implication: Held or moving orbs can skip a shared tick independently of the other spinner cells. The check function itself is not a pure reader and need not be called by the tweak.

claims.claim: The initial grabbed orb is set to state 4; an exchange sets the displaced orb to state 3, swaps orb pointers, and starts movement interpolation on both orbs.
claims.implication: Model token identity and associated orb fields through each swap. A target spinner must reach its desired color before entering it; holding on that cell does not advance its held orb color. The interpolation argument 0.125 alone does not establish a verified eight-frame settle bound.

claims.claim: In the same updater, spinner recoloring precedes orb movement processing; state is cleared to 0 only when interpolation current equals target and state is neither 4 nor 5.
claims.implication: An orb that becomes settled in this update can already have skipped that update's spinner tick. Rebase remaining phase predictions from a native read after exchanges.

claims.claim: The raw-zero ordinary cycle maps colors 0..4 to the next color and a current color above 4 to fire 0. Custom color selection scans the configured color bit table; custom results 6..9 clear enhancement data and flags 0x28000.
claims.implication: Hazard conversion is a real native possibility, but supporting it needs branch-specific color and metadata replay. A normal six-color model must not silently accept an unsupported custom table or leave stale orb metadata.

claims.claim: In the normal phase-2 dispatcher branch, input is processed before the common updater tail.
claims.implication: Input and spinner update can occur in the same game frame. Function address order alone is not execution order; these sites are connected by the dispatcher control flow.

claims.claim: Release cleanup clears an orb flag and conditionally resets state 4. Native matching waits for states 1..3, and for a state-4 orb whose interpolation current differs from target, plus other special-state checks.
claims.implication: Visible release color is not sufficient evidence of the actual match snapshot. A route valid for all allowed terminal phases can avoid relying on a specific release frame, but only if its terminal spinner colors were modeled correctly.

claims.claim: All active cells use the same decoded color mask at impl+0xB4FD0. A nonzero mask selects the next set color bit in ascending color order with wrap; unset colors are skipped within this one tick. Raw zero instead selects the ordinary six-color cycle.
claims.model_comparison: For the supported basic-color subsets (bits 0..5, at least two set, current color in table), PHOrbSpinnerType's ascending next-allowed-color selection matches the native result. The native bit-search sentinel and loop iterations are not extra elapsed frames. ReadSpinner normalizes raw zero to 63; a nonzero subset remains that actual subset.
claims.implication: Do not assume every spinner can supply all six colors. Plan only takes and supported donors inside the current mask, and revoke a pending route when that mask changes. Shared color table still permits per-cell phase differences after held/moving skips.
